Brandon’s available information:

- Brandon is an insurance agent. He meets Benjamin Erickson, an entrepreneur, in a professional setting where Benjamin seeks business insurance advice. Brandon is aware Benjamin has limited formal education, so he is concerned about communicating complex insurance details effectively.
- In the first meeting, Brandon says they should consider comprehensive coverage, including liabilities and assets. He hears Benjamin say he wants everything covered but some terms are new. Brandon explains liability insurance as a safety net, gives a slip-and-fall example, and explains asset protection as guarding inventory and equipment. He hears Benjamin say this simplifies things and thanks him for breaking it down.
- After prior interactions, Brandon revises his belief about Benjamin’s ability to understand detailed information. He now feels more confident and plans to discuss more complex policy details.
- In a subsequent meeting, Brandon introduces detailed policy options. He hears Benjamin say he is ready and has been reading up since their last meeting. Brandon explains business interruption insurance as covering income loss when operations are interrupted, and property insurance as covering damages and theft losses. He hears Benjamin say these coverages sound crucial and reassuring.
- During a casual lunch meeting, Brandon feels insecure about how Benjamin perceives his cautious nature and tries to balance detail with engaging delivery. He tells Benjamin he worries about getting too caught up in details. He hears Benjamin say he appreciates the thoroughness and enjoys lighter moments. Brandon tells a joke about an entrepreneur insuring his taste buds for a million dollars. He hears Benjamin react with fascination and say it makes sense considering the stakes. Brandon says it is about assessing risks, like their business but less unusual. He hears Benjamin agree it is less unusual but equally important.
- Later, Brandon feels pleased by Benjamin’s positive response to his personal anecdotes and decides to offer support beyond insurance. He asks whether Benjamin has considered strategic investments that could lower premiums. He hears Benjamin say he has not but it sounds smart. Brandon suggests upgrading security systems to protect assets and reduce insurance costs. He hears Benjamin call it a win-win and agree to explore it.
- Later, Brandon feels encouraged by their strong rapport and mutual benefits and is optimistic about proposing a joint venture. He proposes co-developing a platform that integrates risk management with financial planning for entrepreneurs. He hears Benjamin call it a groundbreaking idea and say combining their expertise could set them apart. Brandon says they can leverage their strengths to offer something unique. He hears Benjamin agree to draft initial plans.

Brandon has access only to what he directly observed, did, said, heard from Benjamin, or already knew about Benjamin from their professional interactions.
